chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs73706717
predictions: The T and C alleles will not show a reproducible, functionally relevant difference in TF binding caused by this base; any CRC association could instead reflect linkage to another variant or no causal effect.
falsified_if: Precise editing of rs73706717 reproducibly changes TF occupancy and cis MYC regulation in colorectal cells, with the effect dependent on the implicated TF.

chains.title: Candidate TCF7L2-dependent MYC enhancer effect
chains.element: A candidate cis-regulatory element near MYC

links.claim: Hypothesis: the C allele binds TCF7L2 more strongly than the T allele. TCF7L2 is a plausible CRC-context candidate, but no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result for this site is available here, so the direction is untested.
The variant acts in a candidate cis-regulatory element that can influence MYC.
The element increases MYC expression when TCF7L2 binding is greater.
The proposed effect occurs in colorectal epithelial cells, with HCT 116 as a testable context.
Higher MYC activity in colorectal epithelium could increase CRC susceptibility.

predictions: Allele-specific binding assays will show greater TCF7L2 binding to C than T.
Editing T to C will increase TCF7L2 occupancy and MYC expression; reducing TCF7L2 will attenuate the expression difference.
falsified_if: A suitably sensitive assay finds no C-over-T TCF7L2 binding difference.
Precise allele editing produces no TCF7L2-dependent change in MYC regulation.

chains.title: Candidate HNF4A-dependent MYC enhancer effect
chains.element: A candidate cis-regulatory element near MYC

links.claim: Hypothesis: the T allele binds HNF4A more strongly than the C allele. HNF4A is a candidate because of its role in intestinal epithelial gene regulation; no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result for this site is available here.
The variant acts in a candidate cis-regulatory element that can influence MYC.
Greater HNF4A binding increases MYC expression through this element.
The proposed effect occurs in colorectal epithelial cells with HNF4A activity.
A resulting increase in MYC activity could increase CRC susceptibility.

predictions: Allele-specific assays will show greater HNF4A binding to T than C, rather than the C-over-T TCF7L2 pattern proposed in H1.
Editing C to T will increase HNF4A occupancy and HNF4A-dependent MYC expression.
falsified_if: HNF4A does not occupy the region in the relevant cells or shows no T-over-C binding difference.
Allele editing produces no HNF4A-dependent change in MYC regulation.

chains.title: Candidate JUN-dependent enhancer effect
chains.element: A candidate cis-regulatory element near MYC

links.claim: Hypothesis: the C allele binds JUN more strongly than the T allele. JUN is a candidate stress-responsive regulator, but no occupancy or QBiC-SELEX result for this site is available here.
The variant acts in a candidate cis-regulatory element that can influence MYC.
Greater JUN binding increases MYC expression through this element.
The proposed effect occurs in colorectal epithelial cells under conditions with JUN activity.
A resulting increase in MYC activity could increase CRC susceptibility.

predictions: Allele-specific assays will show greater JUN binding to C; JUN perturbation, rather than TCF7L2 or HNF4A perturbation, will remove the allele-dependent MYC effect.
falsified_if: JUN does not occupy the region or shows no C-over-T binding difference.
Allele editing produces no JUN-dependent change in MYC regulation.

matrix.test: Low-cost electrophoretic mobility shift assay using matched T- and C-allele probes and recombinant TCF7L2; compare allele-specific complexes, with specificity controls.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible TCF7L2-specific difference between the two probes; this would be consistent with the null, though it would not rule out other mechanisms.
A reproducibly stronger TCF7L2-specific complex with the C probe than the T probe.
No predicted TCF7L2-specific C-over-T difference; this assay does not directly test the HNF4A model.
No predicted TCF7L2-specific C-over-T difference; this assay does not directly test the JUN model.

next_experiment: Run the low-cost TCF7L2 allele-specific mobility shift assay described above to distinguish the leading null hypothesis from the leading candidate chain. A positive result would test differential binding only, not endogenous occupancy, MYC regulation, or disease causality.
